                    ### Question
                    A section from the thymus of a patient with myasthenia gravis is examined (see image). The function of the portion of the thymus designated by the arrow plays what role in the pathophysiology of this disease?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Failure to bind MHC class II molecules
opb. Failure of hematopoietic progenitor cells to differentiate in thymus
opc. Premature involution of the thymus
opd. Failure of afferent lymph vessels to form
ope. Failure of apoptosis of negatively selected T cells

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In the pathophysiology of myasthenia gravis, the failure of apoptosis of negatively selected T cells leads to the accumulation of autoreactive T cells, triggering an autoimmune response. This process is a key factor in the development of the disease. The premature involution of the thymus can also contribute to dysregulation of immune tolerance, further influencing myasthenia gravis pathogenesis. Relevant evidence suggests that alterations in immune tolerance can lead to the development of myasthenia gravis, supporting the importance of these mechanisms in the disease.
